palette.notes: Code: 8 colours and one 120 deg ramp on the still; looks too low for these lit rooms, not trusted. Day scene: lavender, warm lamp orange; night scenes: neon blue and pink with cool blue shadows.

lighting: Motivated lights: desk lamp and window rain-light by day, neon signs and a glowing monitor at night; the cool night grade is the mood change.
silhouette: Gamer in a chair seen side-on, then slumped asleep facing camera; Pokemon posters and plushies frame him. Busy scenes, so the figure reads by its pose and the dark shirt.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 33.3 ms (p75 66.7 ms), 10.57 changes/s; motion is subtle loops (typing, rain, breathing) inside three nearly static AI-generated scenes.

texture: AI-generated pixel-art style (caption tags #AI): pixel-looking but inconsistent pixel size and soft gradients, so it is pseudo-pixel art.
camera: Static frames; three hard cuts between scenes (typing by day, asleep with 'Lv.99' bubble, asleep in a Pokemon room).

acting.enters: No entrance; each scene opens with the character already in place.
acting.acts: Types at the desk, then sleeps; a 'Lv.99' speech bubble tells the joke.
acting.exits: Hard cut between scenes; no exits.
acting.depth: Character mid-ground, posters and plushies in the back and props on the floor in front; no depth play.

techniques: day-to-night grade change as the story beat
speech bubble with a single word ('Lv.99') as the gag
small idle loops in a static scene
dense prop dressing to set the fandom
feel: busy fan-room dressing + day-to-night cut + one-word bubble = cozy but static; AI pixels lack a clean grid
for_fred: Avoid: still scenes with only idle loops; Fred needs to move between scenes. Borrow the one-word speech bubble and the day-to-night grade shift to mark time passing.
